message.content: {"decision":"PROPOSE","observations":["The attempted solution derives a|105 from divisibility constraints but then asserts a=105 is achievable without constructing or proving existence of an integer-coefficient polynomial.","The key missing step is a necessary condition from evaluating the polynomial at an integer outside 1..8, e.g. x=0 or x=9, using the fact that P(x)-P(y) is divisible by x-y for integer-coefficient P.","A correct approach: from P(0)-P(k) divisible by k for k=1..8, and P(0)-P(k) = P(0) ± a, one obtains congruences on P(0) mod each k; combining with P(0) ≡ a mod odd k and P(0) ≡ -a mod even k yields a strong divisibility condition on a (in fact 2a divisible by lcm-type products), forcing a larger minimum than 105.","The failing operation is the unjustified existence claim for a=105; the replacement is to derive a necessary condition via P(0) (or P(9)) and then verify sufficiency by an explicit construction or CRT argument."],"procedure_plan":"Parameterize by the two disjoint finite sets of integer inputs S+ and S- and the common magnitude a. Algorithm: (1) For each pair (i in S+, j in S-), the condition P(i)-P(j) = 2a divisible by i-j gives 2a ≡ 0 mod |i-j|; collect these into a single modulus M = lcm of all |i-j| (and also handle same-sign pairs trivially). (2) Use the integer-valued polynomial condition at an external point t0 (default 0): for every k in S+ ∪ S-, P(t0)-P(k) is divisible by t0-k. Writing P(t0)=c, this gives c ≡ a mod (t0-k) for k in S+ and c ≡ -a mod (t0-k) for k in S-. Solve this system of congruences in (c,a) via CRT/generalized CRT over the moduli |t0-k|; the resulting congruence on a (a ≡ r mod L, or a constrained to a residue class) yields the true necessary condition. (3) The smallest positive a satisfying all congruences is the candidate; verify sufficiency by checking that the interpolation polynomial through the required values can be taken with integer coefficients (equivalently, that the divided-difference/Newton interpolation values are integers, or construct via CRT lifting). Return the minimal positive a.","uncertainty":"The exact minimal a depends on correctly solving the coupled congruence system in (c,a); the generalized CRT may yield no solution for some residue choices, and sufficiency (existence of an integer-coefficient polynomial) requires an additional argument beyond necessary congruences. The choice of external point t0=0 is standard but t0=9 or others could give equivalent or stronger conditions; the plan assumes the congruence system captures all obstructions, which is true for integer-valued polynomial interpolation but the sufficiency check must be done carefully.","invalid_operation":"Claiming a=105 is achievable solely because no modular obstruction was found among the sampled primes, without constructing an integer-coefficient polynomial or proving existence; the solution never uses evaluation at a point outside {1,...,8}, missing the divisibility condition that actually rules out a=105.","replacement_operation":"Introduce an auxiliary integer c=P(0) (or P(9)) and use the integer-coefficient divisibility property P(0)-P(k) divisible by k for each k in the input set. This produces congruences c ≡ a (mod odd k) and c ≡ -a (mod even k), which when solved jointly impose a stronger condition on a than a|105, yielding the correct minimum. Sufficiency is then established by explicit interpolation/CRT construction.","parameter_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"plus_inputs":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"integer"},"description":"Integer x-values where P(x)=a (e.g. [1,3,5,7])"},"minus_inputs":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"integer"},"description":"Integer x-values where P(x)=-a (e.g. [2,4,6,8])"},"external_point":{"type":"integer","description":"Integer t0 outside the input sets used to derive the extra congruence (default 0)","default":0}},"required":["plus_inputs","minus_inputs"],"additionalProperties":false},"source_parameters":{"plus_inputs":[1,3,5,7],"minus_inputs":[2,4,6,8],"external_point":0}}
